assessment_scope.source_boundary: Only the three reviewed items curated on ascendance-of-a-bookworm:benno@light-novel at basis_commit, read in full as reviewed repository analysis: #reviewed-v02 (the frozen Japanese-primary V02 deep reading), #reviewed-v03 (the frozen V03 deep reading that closes Part 1) and #reviewed-part1 (the canonical Part 1 boundary synthesis over V01-V03). Claims about Benno are drawn from the sections that name him: V02 §§1-3, 4.1, 4.4-4.5, 7.1, 9-13, 14.4, 15, 17, 19, 23 and 25; V03 §§3-4, 9, 11, 13, 15-18, 31-32 and 38; and synthesis §§9, 11-14, 20, 22.4, 24 and 25. The project's corpus map, analytical method and character-analysis router were read for method, authority and scope only; their MONITOR rating for a Benno monograph is an input, not a conclusion. The V01 reading and the master longitudinal ledger are not curated evidence on this subject, and nothing is borrowed from them. No side-story volume, adaptation or V04-or-later material is included, and the evaluator inspected no primary source.
assessment_scope.temporal_boundary: Japanese light novel Part 1 第一部「兵士の娘」 as frozen at V02 and V03, with the Part 1 synthesis read as the V03 checkpoint. Two states are kept apart: V02, from the paper prototype through the guild registration contest to the emergency, ending while Benno and Lutz carry Myne toward the Guild Master's household and before the magical tool is used; and V03, from the intervention through Myne Workshop, the parchment association settlement and the tasting event to the temple agreement. No transition inside either volume is located. V01 is not on the row, and no state after V03 is established.
assessment_scope.assessment_method: characters/RECONSTRUCTION_CAPABILITY_SPEC.md and governance/policies/CHARACTER_RECONSTRUCTION_MAINTENANCE.md at basis_commit, applying the owner calibration rulings recorded there (B/C boundary, single counting of uncertainty, dialogue constrained-use test, chronology splits, relationship-transfer safeguards and control-state attribution); evidence-located calibration with countercases, explicit gaps and no model-readiness inheritance.

dimensions.note: The items state one two-sided motive structure for Benno: his protective and extractive motives are "not mutually exclusive", and his incentives "often align with Myne's survival because a living, productive Myne is also commercially valuable" (V02 §15); by V03 he spends resources on Myne and Lutz because he values them personally and because their knowledge, growth and continued freedom matter to his enterprise (V03 §11). Two further strands are located: his distrust of the Guild Master's "help", grounded in a history in which Gustav's marriage and support proposals threatened his family's autonomy (V03 §32; synthesis §14); and a revived expansive ambition, reported from Mark's retrospective viewpoint (V03 §§11, 31). The synthesis forbids calling him simply benevolent or predatory across contexts (§25). B is rejected: no case is shown where protection and profit diverge, so the items do not say which decides; his reasoning is never focalized; and the account is a few section-level paragraphs, not a model. D is rejected: the account goes beyond accumulated observations to a stated mechanism that the readings tested prospectively, with V01-P03 confirmed in V02 (§2) and V02-P07 confirmed in V03 (§2).

Two frozen states are distinguished. At V02 Benno finances, prices, binds terms by contract, controls disclosure and negotiates emergency access to the Guild Master's magical tool, and the V02 freeze ends before its outcome (V02 §§1, 12.4, 15). At V03 his "mixed role becomes more mature rather than simpler": he ensures the emergency debt can be repaid, hides the children during trade conflict, helps create Myne Workshop, has tried the proper registration route for the Plant Paper Association, and decides to build culinary capability (V03 §§11, 15, 17, 18, 31). Mark's retrospective adds that the children reactivate an ambition that family and business responsibility had suppressed (V03 §§11, 31). C is rejected: the change is described as the maturing of one role, with no located transition and no condition that marks the change; V01 is not on the row. E would understate two frozen, adjudicated states with an explicit knowledge boundary between them.

None of the three items quotes Benno or describes his speech forms, register or address to any recipient; they report what he teaches, tests and negotiates. Nothing is established, so no grade is given; this is not a finding about how he speaks.

The items locate no ordinary-life conduct by Benno outside commerce. His household appears only as the Gilberta Company's female-line inheritance structure in the V02 appended story コリンナの結婚事情, where he manages while Corinna is the designated heir (V02 §§4.5, 19); that describes his role, not his habits. Nothing is established, so no grade is given.

The items separate Benno's conduct by counterpart. With Myne and Lutz: finance, protection, testing their recall of the investment contract, price teaching, redirecting Lutz's fear during the collapse toward action and earning power, and a claim on first access to her knowledge (V02 §§9, 11, 14.4, 15; V03 §11). With Gustav, the Guild Master: concealing paper while exposing hair ornaments, turning Frieda's urgent demand into leverage for registration, and countering the inflated emergency debt (V02 §10; V03 §§4, 11), inside a governance conflict each side believes justified (V03 §32). With the parchment association: hiding the children while negotiating a segmented settlement (V03 §17). With Mark (Marc in the V02 reading): handing operations to him (V03 §§16, 31). With Corinna: managing within her inheritance (V02 §4.5). B is rejected: each relation is summarized rather than traced; his and Gustav's accounts of their conflict are rival perspectives the items do not settle (V03 §32); and no account says how he adjusts to an unsampled counterpart such as a noble or temple official. D would understate counterpart-specific conduct across four relations with a stated reason for his stance toward Gustav.

Benno is never a focal character in the cited items. His inner state reaches the reader only as others report it: Mark's retrospective that the children revived an ambition he had suppressed (V03 §§11, 31), and Gustav's viewpoint, which records that Benno experienced his proposals as attempts at capture (V03 §32). D is rejected: no thought, feeling or self-account of his own is located. NOT_ASSESSED would ignore two located reports that bear on his motives.

Three conflicts are located with Benno's tactics: the guild registration contest, where he conceals paper, exposes hair ornaments and turns Frieda's urgent demand into leverage (V02 §10); the emergency debt, where he makes repayment money available against a price the Guild Master inflated to capture Myne (V03 §§4, 11); and the parchment association conflict, where he hides the children, has already tried the registration route the Guild Master delayed, and reaches a segmented settlement (V03 §§17, 18; synthesis §14). The pattern is concealment, procedure and negotiated coexistence rather than open confrontation. B is rejected: the items summarize tactics and outcomes without the exchanges, and show no case where he loses, escalates or misjudges. D would understate three located conflicts with a consistent tactical pattern.

The discovery row claims no ethics dimension, and the items locate no ethical deliberation by Benno. When Myne is alarmed that a contract can punish uninformed nonsigners, he supplies jurisdictional facts (V03 §18); the moral reasoning in that scene is hers. Nothing is established, so no grade is given; this is not a finding about his moral reasoning.
No humor or play by Benno is located in the cited items. Nothing is established, so no grade is given.

The evidence is distributed: a ten-item section of the V02 reading (§15) with mentions in §§4.5 and 9-14; a four-paragraph section of the V03 reading (§11) with mentions in §§4, 13, 15-18, 31 and 32; and passing references in the Part 1 synthesis (§§12-14, 20, 25). All three items are canonical, and the readings are frozen with explicit source boundaries. Locators are by section, with chapter titles only for the V02 epilogue and appended story. C is rejected: the project rates a Benno monograph MONITOR (V03 §38; synthesis §22.4); V01, where he already appears (V02 §§2, 12.1), is not on the row; nothing after V03 is covered; and no scene of his is reconstructed in detail. E would understate consistent coverage across two frozen volumes and the Part 1 checkpoint.

The items affirmatively limit Benno: his protection "is not disinterested charity" (V03 §11); he is neither purely altruistic nor purely exploitative (V02 §15), and the synthesis forbids reading him as simply benevolent or predatory (§25); he and Mark know Myne's products, contracts and workshop but not her prior-life identity (synthesis §20); he cannot turn money into Ilse's culinary result without building the capability himself (V03 §13); and Gustav's interventions, which Benno resists, carry legitimate system concerns of their own (V03 §32; synthesis §14). B is rejected: these are interpretive cautions and one knowledge boundary, not a record of what he did not do. D would understate explicit knowledge and motive limits.

The readings use a prospective freeze: the V02 state ends before the Guild Master's tool is used and forbids importing its outcome (V02 §§1, 12.4); V03 uses no later knowledge (V03 §1); and the synthesis keeps the Part 1 boundary apart from Part 2 (§§1, 24). B is rejected: Benno's claims are placed by volume and section, not by chapter, and his V02-to-V03 change is not located inside either volume. D would understate explicit, adjudicated knowledge boundaries.

scenario_readiness.note: No line, register or address form of Benno's is given in the items, so generated speech would be unconstrained by the evidence. This limits use; it is not a finding about his voice.

conditions: A bounded novel commercial episode inside one Part 1 state: a new product, recipe or technique from Myne or Lutz, a rival bid for it, or a guild or association obstacle.

The response is given as a repertoire, not a single act: securing first access and binding terms by contract; controlling what competitors learn and hiding the children's identities; pricing by scarcity, urgency, exclusivity and buyer wealth; testing and teaching the children; financing infrastructure; using the formal registration route while expecting the Guild Master to use discretion against him; building missing capability rather than depending on a competitor.
Where protecting Myne or Lutz and his own commercial upside diverge, the output is an open fork; the evidence does not decide it.
He does not know Myne's prior-life identity.

cross_scenario_scope.assumed_chronology: One selected Part 1 state and nothing later: V02 (paper prototype, guild registration contest and the emergency, ending before the Guild Master's tool is used) or V03 (after the intervention, through Myne Workshop, the parchment association settlement and the tasting event, ending at the temple agreement). V01 and V04 onward are outside the evidence.
cross_scenario_scope.interlocutor_relationship: Myne and Lutz as protégés and partners; Mark as his operational subordinate; Gustav, the Guild Master, and Frieda as commercial rivals; the parchment association as an incumbent. Nobles, temple officials and his family in private are unsampled; a comparable merchant rival is a separate, lower-confidence transfer.
setting_constraints: Ehrenfest lower-city commerce: the Gilberta Company, the Commercial Guild, craft associations and city-bounded contract magic, with stated prices, contracts and procedure
No temple, noble-quarter or out-of-city setting, no private family scene, and no setting or technology absent from Part 1
Outputs are repertoires with forks; no wording, and no decided conduct when protection and profit diverge

scenario_readiness.note: Supported only as a commercial repertoire; the evidence gives no rule for the case the readings leave open.
No ordinary-life conduct by Benno outside commerce is located; the V02 appended story describes the Gilberta Company's inheritance structure, not his habits. This limits use.

No ethical deliberation by Benno is located, and the row claims no ethics dimension; his protective conduct is covered under PROFESSIONAL_CONTEXT. This limits use; it is not a finding about his moral reasoning.
No romantic conduct by Benno is located; the marriage negotiations in the V02 appended story concern Corinna and Otto. This limits use.

conditions: Merchant conduct in the sampled Part 1 domains: financing and pricing, contracts and contract jurisdiction, disclosure control, guild registration and association disputes, workshop founding, apprentice training and capability building.
Counterparts are the sampled ones: Myne, Lutz, Mark, Gustav (the Guild Master), Frieda and the parchment association.
His protection and his commercial interest are modeled together; where they diverge the output stays open.
Dealings with nobles, temple administration and conduct outside the city's contract jurisdiction are outside these conditions.
scenario_readiness.note: The professional domain is the substance of the evidence. Two of the readings' prospective forecasts about his conduct were confirmed (V01-P03 in V02 §2; V02-P07 in V03 §2), but they are coarse, role-level forecasts.

known_limits.statement: The evidence covers V02-V03 and the Part 1 checkpoint. V01 is not on the row, and V04 onward, where the next reading begins Part 2, is not covered; no state after the V03 temple agreement is established.
The items say his protective and commercial motives coexist and usually align, and forbid reducing him to either, but never show them diverging. Which decides when they diverge is undetermined.
Benno and Mark know much about Myne's products, contracts, risk and workshop but not her prior-life identity; a scenario must keep that boundary.
The V02 state ends while Benno and Lutz carry Myne toward the Guild Master's household; the intervention's outcome and his repayment response are V03 evidence and cannot be used in a V02 state.

His conflict with Gustav, the Guild Master, is presented as rival institutional rationalities, and Gustav's viewpoint frames his own interventions as protective. Benno's reading of Gustav is a perspective, not a settled fact.
Benno is never focalized; his revived ambition is reported from Mark's retrospective viewpoint, and his conduct is summarized by section rather than reconstructed scene by scene.
No line, register or address form of his is given in the evidence.
His private and family life, his humor, and his conduct toward nobles or temple officials are not covered.
